note: P4321 (Pro 28:11) — a rich man is wise in his own eyes; a discerning poor man finds him out.

dims.v: self-conceit — the rich man's flattering self-estimate
the rich man's conceit of his own wisdom — wealth breeding a flattering self-estimate that a discerning poor man easily sees through
the poor man's discernment that exposes it (266541)
set against the true understanding that finds him out
chakam (wise, in his own eyes) — 'a rich man is WISE in his own eyes'; wealth tempts a man to overrate his own wisdom. Riches flatter the self, but do not confer discernment (cf 26:12; 28:26).
true understanding — the poor man who sees through the rich man's conceit
the understanding of a poor man who searches out and exposes the self-conceited rich — true discernment, unbought by wealth, that sees a man for what he is
set against the rich man's flattering self-estimate

bin (understand/discern) — 'but a poor man who has UNDERSTANDING will find him out'; real discernment, which wealth cannot buy, sees through the rich man's self-conceit. Understanding is no respecter of purses.
